The seat and the moment

Harbor watch officer. Harbor Night.

An unauthorized autonomous vehicle is in a working harbor. Sonar says "something is there." Nobody knows what, or whose.

Today's answer

Close the berth.

Every unknown contact becomes a shutdown, a page, or both.

Across our scenario catalog, closing the berth on every contact cost 1,293 shutdown-minutes and 433 false shutdowns (simulated, stress-test).

What sits between "seen" and "handled"

What a small, low-cost platform decides alone, and what a person must approve.

Soundings asks first.

The organizers' ladder

watch → ask → slow → hold → hand to a person

  1. watchtrack, score, compare with the harbor's pattern of life
  2. →
  3. we live hereaskregistry lookup and an acoustic hail: most contacts clear here
  4. →
  5. slowan advisory for one basin, under signed standing orders
  6. →
  7. holdone gate or berth, bounded in time, under signed standing orders
  8. →
  9. we live herehand to a persona SITREP with its evidence; the person decides

We live on ask and hand to a person.

Watch is the floor. Slow and hold run only under signed standing orders, scoped to one basin or one berth. Everything after the handoff is a person's call.

Two lives, one system
Tuesday

A flight plan for the water

Research AUV teams, hull-cleaning divers and inspectors file a plan. Their contact clears at ask with no one interrupted. A filed vehicle that goes silent gets a search box.

Who pays: the harbor department (fewer false alarms, divers kept clear of traffic) and the operators (a registry, and lost-vehicle finding).

Harbor Night

Who is safer

Unfiled, closing on the fuel berth, no reply to the hail. Hold one berth under signed standing orders; the report with its evidence goes to the officer, who decides.

At night with the network down: the node runs at the edge, the report queues for whoever is reachable, nothing escalates on its own.

We lean crisis. Every Tuesday contact is a rehearsal.

Soundings resolved 68.9% of catalog contacts at or below ask (simulated detection, stress-test estimate).

Slow when the threat mass is at least 0.25 and a critical asset is under 600 s away. Hold when it is at least 0.35, under 300 s, zone criticality at least 0.7, with at most 0 other holds active. Hand to a person at a threat mass of 0.35. Stress-test settings, not forecasts.

Deterministic guards decide every transition over a typed evidence table. Model output never sets a rung, a threshold, or an approval.

What it runs on · feasibility

Sense · ask · decide · hand off

Sense

Hydrophone node: tracks and acoustic features into a typed evidence table. Simulated this weekend.

Ask

Registry of planned underwater work (a web form) and an acoustic challenge-response hail.

model: proposes the next probe only

Decide

A hand-rolled state machine with deterministic guards and signed standing orders.

model: proposes hypotheses only

Hand off

A SITREP where every line links to its evidence row; SMS or queue to whoever is reachable.

model: drafts the SITREP only

Honesty and responsible use

What this is, and what it is not

simulated Detection is simulated: one card per model, every value a demo value with its source in config/physics.yaml.

Passive sonar detection

p = p_max * health * logistic((SL - TL - NL - DT) / k), TL = 20 log10(r) + alpha r; none beyond max_range_factor x the calm-noise effective range
  • alpha db per km 1 dB/km
  • detection threshold db 21.4 dB
  • logistic k db 2 dB
  • max range factor 2 ratio
  • source level db biologic 130 dB re 1 uPa at 1 m
  • source level db propeller tonal absent 130 dB re 1 uPa at 1 m
  • source level db propeller tonal present 130 dB re 1 uPa at 1 m

Ambient noise

NL = 10 log10(10^(NL_base/10) + 10^(NL_sea/10) + sum_i 10^(L_i/10)), L_i = SL_v - falloff x log2(max(d_i, d_ref) / d_ref)
  • ambient noise base db 55 dB re 1 uPa^2/Hz
  • sea state default 1 Beaufort-style sea state
  • sea state table 0 44.5 dB re 1 uPa^2/Hz
  • sea state table 1 50 dB re 1 uPa^2/Hz
  • sea state table 2 55 dB re 1 uPa^2/Hz
  • sea state table 3 58 dB re 1 uPa^2/Hz
  • sea state table 4 60 dB re 1 uPa^2/Hz
  • vessel noise falloff db per doubling 6.02 dB per doubling of distance
  • vessel noise reference distance m 1 m
  • vessel noise source level db 100 dB re 1 uPa^2/Hz at 1 m

Hail latency

t_reply = t_turnaround + 2r / c
  • modem turnaround s 18.9 s
  • sound speed mps 1,500 m/s

Camera visibility

V = V_hour * exp(-k * depth) * exp(-turbidity); fog gives 0
  • k depth per m 0.05 1/m
  • turbidity default 0 optical depth

Responder battery drain

drain_min = drain_coeff * v^3 * dt
  • drain coeff 0 min of battery per (m/s)^3 per s

What we do not model: hydrodynamics, beam patterns, multipath, bottom type, frequency-dependent spectra, real signal processing, array gain, sensor clock drift, rain and biologic choruses, vessel speed or size dependence, modem protocol, reply authentication, glare and surface waves, artificial lighting, current set and drift on the hull, battery temperature.

stress-test Probabilities are stress-test estimates from a declared, visible catalog, not operational forecasts.

scope The work stops at the handoff. Physically stopping a vehicle is out of scope by the sponsor's brief.

No recorded probe_planner fixtures were used in this run; every LLM-planner call fell back to the deterministic planner, so outcomes are identical by construction. The LLM layer added nothing measurable here.

Responsible-use note

Misuse: surveilling swimmers or divers outside designated security zones, or using the output to justify autonomous action against a person.

Limits: geofenced to declared zones; no identity inference; nothing above the signed standing-orders scope executes without a named human's approval; the system's work ends at the handoff; immutable audit log; 30-day retention.
